content.title: About
content.content: Sorghum flour is made from milled sorghum grains that have been pre‑gelatinized, making it instantly soluble in water. The product is certified organic, grown without synthetic pesticides or GMOs. It has a mild, slightly nutty flavor and a light‑yellow color, ideal for gluten‑free recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sorghum is one of the most drought‑tolerant cereals, cultivated in arid regions of Africa and Asia.
Pre‑gelatinized flour swells quickly, simplifying its use in sauces, porridges, and baked goods without long soaking.
Organic production guarantees no synthetic fertilizers or pesticides were used.
Sorghum flour is naturally gluten‑free, safe for people with celiac disease.
Sorghum has a long culinary history, featuring in Indian (porridge) and African (fufu) dishes.

items.title: Rich in complex carbohydrates
items.content: Provides slowly digestible carbs that help maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Good source of dietary fiber
items.content: High fiber content supports digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains iron and magnesium
items.content: These minerals are essential for blood formation and normal muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds in sorghum help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Gluten‑free
items.content: Suitable for gluten‑free diets, reducing the risk of reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Cereal allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to sorghum, ranging from skin rashes to gastrointestinal symptoms.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Like most flours, sorghum flour is calorie‑dense; portion control is important for weight management.

items.title: Oxalate content
items.content: Contains modest levels of oxalates, which may be a concern for people prone to kidney stones.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use the pre‑gelatinized sorghum flour in gluten‑free breads, pancakes, muffins, or as a thickener for sauces, soups, and porridges. Its quick solubility also makes it easy to stir into cold drinks, smoothies, and yogurt.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For longer shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent fat oxidation.
